events.title: Jim Gray receives Turing Award
events.summary: Jim Gray won the 1998 ACM [Turing Award] for contributions to database and transaction processing — foundational work on [ACID] reliability.
events.about: Gray's transaction processing research underpins every bank transfer and e-commerce checkout. He also championed data-intensive science and disappeared at sea in 2007 during a sailing trip.

narrative.whyChosen: Gray defined how reliable databases handle concurrent transactions.
narrative.whyImportant: [ACID] transactions became the guarantee behind financial and enterprise software.
narrative.problemSolved: Concurrent database access risked inconsistent state without formal transaction models.

events.title: Sutton RL textbook published
events.summary: Richard Sutton and Andrew Barto published [reinforcement learning]: An Introduction in 1998 — the foundational textbook for RL theory and practice.
events.about: Sutton's temporal-difference learning and policy-gradient frameworks became the vocabulary for game-playing agents, [robotics], and later DeepMind's AlphaGo. The book's second edition in 2018 updated decades of RL progress.

narrative.whyChosen: Sutton's textbook codified [reinforcement learning] as a teachable discipline.
narrative.whyImportant: It trained researchers who built modern game-playing and [robotics] AI.
narrative.problemSolved: RL ideas were scattered across papers without a unified pedagogical framework.
